cover letter
Bachelor's degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Master's or PhD in public health, social work, public policy, or another related area.
Previous experience working in county human services or related settings.
Prior experience submitting and maintaining Institutional Review Board (IRB) protocols for human subjects research.
Demonstrated experience collecting and analyzing social science data, utilizing qualitative and/or quantitative methods, including surveys, focus groups, and qualitative interviews.
Prior experience with overseeing or managing meeting coordination and logistics (e.g., with hotel/conference facilities).
Experience with program evaluation.

Proficient in the use of Qualtrics, Google Forms, and/or other tools for data gathering; experience with quantitative analytical software such as STATA or R; and/or qualitative analytical software, such as Dedoose, NVIVO, or Atlas.ti.
At least one year of full-time experience working on social science or health research projects.
Prior experience training and/or supervising staff.

The BASSC Research Coordinator & Partnerships Director provides leadership and oversight for the Bay Area Social Services Consortium (BASSC). This position is responsible for high-level oversight, coordination, and conduct of practice research activities for BASSC. Additionally, the BASSC Research Coordinator & Partnerships Director manages agency partner relations, providing leadership and oversight of staff functions, including planning, organizing, arranging, and facilitating regular meetings and retreats for BASSC Partners. These partners include county human services agency executive directors, deans and directors of Bay Area schools of Social work, and a range of staff across these groups who come together to address cross-regional policy and program issues. This position reports to the Mack Center Director, who also serves as the BASSC faculty director.

Lead practice research activities, including gathering and analyzing qualitative or quantitative data; preparing and summarizing information and/or recommendations, engaging with practice research partners and other stakeholders to co-construct interpretation of research results.

Leading or overseeing development of protocols and systems needed to engage in research activities such as IRB applications, amendments, or renewals; participant recruitment and consent; secure storage of administrative data, etc.

Collaborate with BASSC team members, BASSC Agency and University Directors, and their designated staff, to ensure research projects are coordinated and linked effectively with other BASSC work, including workforce development activities, e.g., via supporting translation of results into content for professional development programming.
Lead project planning and partner engagement activities, including leading planning, overseeing, and executing quarterly high-level executive meetings and other meetings as needed.

Specific tasks may include: Lead various forms of meeting coordination, event coordination, project calendar management, and high-level administrative support; Improve and develop technical and other systems, and interpret, monitor, and analyze information regarding policies and procedures, as well as provide recommendations.
Provide reporting at BASSC meetings and represent BASSC research at committee and external stakeholder meetings.
Provide support to meeting co-chairs for meeting agenda preparation, facilitation, and the arrangement of special guest speakers.

Oversee the coordination and logistics of practical support at meetings (e.g., selecting menu options, ordering food, and overseeing event plans such as room setup, audio/visual needs, interfacing with hotel/conference facilities, etc.).

Disseminate BASSC practice research via reports, manuscripts, presentations, or other deliverables and collaborate with BASSC team and agency partners to develop new initiatives informed by study results, including analysis of opportunities for collaborative initiatives with community partners and as appropriate, sponsored research with third-party partners.

Serves as work lead for BASSC staff, Student Research Assistants, and Graduate Student Researchers: assigns and reviews daily work, provides day-to-day guidance and training, and provides feedback to the supervisor for performance reviews.
Adaptable to quickly changing priorities.
Able to travel up to 20% time and work occasional evenings.
Knowledge of county human service agencies, including a nuanced understanding of organizational structures, services provided, and client, community, and workforce characteristics.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with agency partners, community stakeholders, study participants, and individuals with a wide range of racial, ethnic, and educational backgrounds.
Broad academic knowledge and applied background in social services research, proven by successful planning, initiation, execution, and reporting of previous investigations.
Demonstrated ability to analyze, research, and synthesize large amounts of data and/or other information with strong attention to detail.
Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities, prioritize projects, and meet the demands of a fast-paced and dynamic work environment.
Ability to problem solve, troubleshoot, and use sound judgment in responding to complex issues and concerns.
Active listening, critical thinking, multi-tasking, and time management skills.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.

Strong ability and willingness to work collaboratively with a small team within a larger University setting, and the ability to learn to flexibly and independently manage tasks, and collaboratively share information to support the collective work of the Consortium. This may mean problem-solving on a wide range of topics and working with a wide range of individuals with sensitivity, thoughtfulness, and care.
Ability to take initiative and solve problems independently while understanding when to seek guidance from a manager or others.
Proficient in the ability to multitask with demanding timeframes while maintaining a calm, capable, and pleasant demeanor with colleagues and stakeholders.

Ability to collaborate effectively and professionally with multiple internal stakeholders, external partners, and consultants; requires political acumen, strong relationship management skills, and attention to confidentiality.
